subject: Logs governance pilot — scope questions (trace IDs & retention)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Aria Kundra <aria.k@equinoxhealth.com>
Cc: security@equinoxhealth.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: logs governance pilot — trace IDs & retention

Hi Aria,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to understand Equinox's inbound/outbound logging model and the privacy constraints for your care platform. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the pilot and demo: 

Recap
- Pilot intent: validate Redwood's ability to deliver sanitized request/response audit streams to your analytics stack while meeting retention and residency requirements.
- Target scope: 1 service (ingest API) -> 30 days of production-like traffic for functional validation and cost/latency profiling.
- Key asks from you: sample logs (anonymized if needed), retention policy, list of headers/tokens considered sensitive.

Clarifying questions (please confirm)
1) Trace identifier handling: do you require full removal of trace IDs from exported logs, or is irreversible hashing/pseudonymization acceptable? If hashing is acceptable, do you need a specified hash algorithm (SHA-256) or HMAC with a per-customer salt?
2) Retention: you mentioned 90 days for internal audit copies — is that the upper bound for the pilot artifact we produce, or should we show a configuration that supports both 30- and 90-day retention tiers?
3) Headers & PII: attached is a simple pii_logging_matrix.csv — can you annotate which header keys and payload fields must be redacted vs pseudonymized vs retained?

Proposed next steps
- If hashing is acceptable, Redwood can enable a traceid-hash filter at export that replaces trace IDs with a one-way digest. This preserves uniqueness for joinability while removing plaintext identifiers.
- If removal is required, we can configure an export-time scrub that drops the field entirely (affects cross-request debugging).
- I can schedule a 30-minute technical pilot kickoff with Sean (solutions) and Marissa (AM) — would Monday May 12 at 10:00 PT work?

Attachments: pii_logging_matrix.csv

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your compliance team's input.

Best,

Thanks Neha — appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline below.

On Fri, May 9, 2026 at 3:12 PM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Recap
> - Pilot intent: validate Redwood's ability to deliver sanitized request/response audit streams to your analytics stack while meeting retention and residency requirements.

Agree. Our primary risk vector is accidental exposure in logs (headers and request bodies).

> Clarifying questions (please confirm)
> 1) Trace identifier handling: do you require full removal of trace IDs from exported logs, or is irreversible hashing/pseudonymization acceptable? If hashing is acceptable, do you need a specified hash algorithm (SHA-256) or HMAC with a per-customer salt?

We prefer irreversible hashing (pseudonymization) so we can still correlate events for debugging on our side. HMAC with a customer-specific salt is preferred (so if logs are ever exported outside our environment they can't be trivially re-identified). SHA-256 alone is acceptable if HMAC would require more engineering on your side.

> 2) Retention: you mentioned 90 days for internal audit copies — is that the upper bound for the pilot artifact we produce, or should we show a configuration that supports both 30- and 90-day retention tiers?

For the pilot, please demonstrate both: 30 days for short-term operational logs and a 90-day tier for audit copies. We will evaluate costs and approvals after the pilot.

> 3) Headers & PII: attached is a simple pii_logging_matrix.csv — can you annotate which header keys and payload fields must be redacted vs pseudonymized vs retained?

I'll have security annotate the matrix by EOD Monday. Expect a few extra fields: x-client-ssn, x-insurance-id, and raw_request_body -> redact. Trace IDs -> pseudonymize (HMAC).

Pilot kickoff: Monday May 12 at 10:00 PT works for us. I'll invite our security engineer (security@equinoxhealth.com).

Also: can you share SOC 2 Type II evidence or point to your compliance package?

Thanks — looking forward.
Aria

Equinox Health

Neha / Marissa / Aria — Thanks — short feasibility summary below.

On Mon, May 11, 2026 at 8:15 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Feasibility: can Redwood's export pipeline support per-customer HMAC of trace IDs during export without retaining the salt in exported artifacts?

Yes — we can support per-customer HMAC at export time. Implementation notes:
- We perform the transform in the export worker; the salt is only present in the control plane config and is not written to exported logs.
- We can support HMAC-SHA256 with a per-customer key (recommended). This preserves uniqueness for correlation while preventing brute-force re-identification.

> Retention tiers: can we produce two parallel export targets (operational: 30d, audit: 90d) and apply redaction rules differently per target?

Yes. Export pipeline supports multiple sinks with independent retention and transform policies. Operational sink: aggressive redaction + 30d retention. Audit sink: pseudonymization + 90d retention. Notes: audit sink will contain pseudonymized trace IDs and encrypted metadata; we can also support access controls via RBAC.

> KV cache / streaming concerns
- The per-request KV cache is internal to the serving runtime and is not exported. Our transforms run on the export worker that accepts the post-serve stream. There is negligible latency impact (sub-5ms per exported event) — should be fine for Equinox pilot volumes.

> Next steps
1) Vendor/compliance pack: Neha, I'll attach the SOC 2 pointer doc to the HubSpot deal.
2) For the pilot we need: annotated pii_logging_matrix.csv from Equinox, 1 hour of representative sample logs (S3/secure share), and a signed SOW.
3) I'll prepare a short demo for May 12 kickoff (10:00 PT) showing config toggles (remove vs HMAC) and a live run with a small sample.

Attachments: none in this reply — I will upload the compliance pointer and demo deck to the drive link shared in the thread.
